NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493,
  2498, 2499, 2503, 2505, 2507, 2512, 2519, and 2521, due to the continuing state of emergency, including
  masking and social distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is
  being broadcast via teleconference. Members of the public may participate in-person in the Council
  Chambers, or virtually in the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling 1-669-900-6833 from any phone, Meeting
  ID: 886 6574 6571, Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using
  the call in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 886 6574 6571, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

minutes_text:
MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 27 2022

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZERUNYAN at 7:06 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall and remotely via
teleconference, in accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), due to the continuing state
of emergency, including masking and social distancing directives as a result of the threat of
the COVID-19 virus.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by an unnamed member of the public.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit

4.  CEREMONIAL

None.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, TO
  APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-H AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  SPECIAL CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 13, 2022

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

C.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 13, 2022

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

D.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF SEPTEMBER 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
SEPTEMBER 27, 2022
 E.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF AUGUST 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF AUGUST 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

G.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION TO AUTHORIZE THE CONTINUED USE OF
  TELECONFERENCE ACCESSIBILITY PROCEDURES TO CONDUCT PUBLIC
  MEETINGS PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361

  ADOPTED RESOLUTION 2530 TO AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO
  CONTINUE TO IMPLEMENT AND UTILIZE TELECONFERENCE
  ACCESSIBILITY PROCEDURES TO CONDUCT PUBLIC MEETINGS
  PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361.

H.  ADJOURNED PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 6, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

A.  SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA

Public comment was received by Gat and Gerald Lum, thanking the City Council for the
Certificate of Recognition presented to Gerald for his 34 years of service to the City on the
Traffic & Safety Committee.

Public comment related to the Promenade and the Palos Verdes Performing Arts (PVPA) was
received by: Ulrike Ziegner Hokanson, Elana Landau, Stefanie & Sadie Sanders, Elizabeth &
Montana Birkett, Monica De La Cruz Povolo, Sophia Galletti, Danny Ryan, Helen Chung, Sally
Stoler, Elise Vu and Katrina Von Kriegenbergh.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PROPOSED ORDINANCE ADOPTING MUNICIPAL CODE AMENDMENTS
  REGARDING: (1) UPDATE TO CHAPTER 17.76 (DENSITY BONUS AND OTHER
  INCENTIVES), (2) AMENDMENTS TO CHAPTER 17.30 (COMMERCIAL-GENERAL
  DISTRICT) TO PROVIDE FOR BONUS LEVEL DEVELOPMENT, AND (3) NEW
  CHAPTER 17.82 (DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENTS)

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) conduct the public hearing on the ordinance
  adopting the proposed zoning code amendments; 2) vote to introduce the ordinance for
  first reading; and 3) direct that the ordinance be brought for a second reading and
  adoption at the next regular City Council meeting.

City Attorney Don Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, TO
  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN so ordered.

City Attorney Davis explained that the 25% community benefit number listed in the report is
a target, the exact number will be negotiated, and that the applicant will select the appraiser
while the City provides direction as to how they approach the evaluation, in response to
COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN’s questions.

Discussion ensued about the process of selecting an appraiser.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN noted that he feels “art” should be removed because it
is too subjective.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
SEPTEMBER 27, 2022
 COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA inquired about the parking requirement language in section
17.76.050, as it relates to recent legislation that was passed to not require parking within a
high-quality transit area. City Attorney Davis stated that he would look into the latest
legislation, noting that we can more easily remove things from the City’s Municipal Code
than add to it.

City Attorney Davis explained that Rolling Hills Estates does not have a major transit stop
within the City, so certain sections would not be applicable, in response to MAYOR PRO
TEM HUFF.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email, via eComment, and
during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social
media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, TO
  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN so ordered.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  INTRODUCE ORDINANCE NO. 744 FOR FIRST READING AND DIRECTED
  THAT THE ORDINANCE BE BROUGHT FOR A SECOND READING AND
  ADOPTION AT THE NEXT REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  NORTHGATE ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT INC. MASTER PROFESSIONAL
  SERVICES AGREEMENT (MPSA) FOR CONTINUED WATER QUALITY
  MONITORING SERVICES AT THE PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER (PWEC)
  FOR FIVE YEARS (2022-27)

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve a five-year Master Professional
  Services Agreement with Northgate Environmental Management Inc. to provide
  consulting services for continued water quality monitoring at the Peter Weber
  Equestrian Center in the not-to-exceed grand total amount of $108,285, all to the
  satisfaction of the City Attorney.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

Consultant Nicky Robinson, Senior Engineer of Northgate Environmental Management,
explained that a 3% rate increase was included in the proposal, in response to COUNCIL
MEMBER STEGURA. She also noted that wet weather monitoring is also done with the City
of Torrance, whose contract is extending for one more year and anticipated to be renewed, but
since it is not guaranteed the rates are higher in the proposal for years two through five.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba and City Attorney Davis explained
that the contract will have the option to terminate at any time, in response to COUNCIL
MEMBER SCHMITZ.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email, via eComment, and
during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social
media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
SEPTEMBER 27, 2022
   APPROVE A FIVE-YEAR MASTER PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT WITH NORTHGATE ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT INC.
  TO PROVIDE CONSULTING SERVICES FOR CONTINUED WATER
  QUALITY MONITORING AT THE PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER
  IN THE NOT-TO-EXCEED GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $108,285, ALL TO
  THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, to
  adjourn to the Pepper Tree Foundation Board Meeting.

**ADJOURN TO PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BOARD MEETING**

A.  PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION FUNDRAISING COMMITTEE APPOINTMENTS

  Recommendation: That the Rolling Hills Estates Pepper Tree Foundation Board of
  Directors appoint the following individuals to the Fundraising Committee: Eileen Hupp,
  Robert Medawar, Julia Parton-Rosas, Lisa Pope and Suzy Zimmerman.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email, via eComment, and
during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social
media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  BOARD MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by VICE-CHAIR HUFF, AS
  FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPOINT THE FOLLOWING INDIVIDUALS TO THE PEPPER TREE
  FOUNDATION FUNDRAISING COMMITTEE: EILEEN HUPP, ROBERT
  MEDAWAR, JULIA PARTON-ROSAS, LISA POPE AND SUZY ZIMMERMAN.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, to reconvene the City Council Meeting.

**RECONVENE CITY COUNCIL MEETING**

B.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER (VERBAL
  REPORT)

City Manager Grammer reported that Los Angeles County remains in the low transmission
level. He also reported that last Friday, Los Angeles County Department of Public Health
revised the Health Order to no longer require masks on public transportation or public transit
areas. He added that the updated booster shots are now available for those 12 years and older.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

City Attorney Don Davis reported that new legislation has been passed affecting the Brown
Act, and that he would provide more details at a future meeting.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF reported that the Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber of Commerce
will be holding its annual Legislative Forum & Luncheon on Monday, October 3 at 11:30 a.m.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 27, 2022
 MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF also reported that the City Celebration on September 17 was a
successful and fun event for the community.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

MAYOR ZERUNYAN reported that he would be attending the California Contract Cities
Association’s (CCCA) Fall Educational Seminar in Lake Arrowhead, along with Management
Analyst Jessica Slawson.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN also reported that CCCA would be holding its annual City Manager’s
Summit on October 27.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2)
  Significant exposure to litigation: one potential case

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

B.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Government Code Section 54957
  Title: City Manager (Annual Evaluation)

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:17 p.m. MAYOR ZERUNYAN adjourned the City Council meeting to Tuesday, October
11, 2022, at 7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a Regular Meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Frank V. Zerunyan
City Clerk  Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
SEPTEMBER 27, 2022
